source_title: Vesuvius Annual Report and Financial Statements 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 75 and 145 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board and Directors on 27 February 2020; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue fell 4.9% to £1,710.4m, trading profit declined 8.0% to £181.4m, return on sales contracted 40bps to 10.6% and profit before tax fell 24.1% to £118.6m amid sharply deteriorating steel and foundry markets. Against this, cash conversion reached 120%, free cash flow was £121.5m and like-for-like net debt fell to £216.3m, with leverage low at 1.1x.
already_announced_exclusion: The accelerated manufacturing-network optimisation, eight plant closures, support-function efficiencies and restructuring savings disclosed and implemented before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Broad sales and profit deterioration and accelerated restructuring create material pressure. Exceptional cash conversion, strong free cash flow, falling underlying debt and low leverage provide substantial contrary evidence.

source_title: Vesuvius Annual Report and Financial Statements 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report PDF pages 52 and 89 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board and Directors on 3 March 2022; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 12.7% to £1,642.9m, trading profit increased 40.4% to £142.4m, return on sales expanded 170bps to 8.7% and profit before tax nearly doubled to £127.6m. Rapid growth and investment absorbed working capital, reducing free cash flow to a £0.3m outflow and increasing net debt to £277.1m and leverage to 1.4x, but interest cover remained 30.5x and committed liquidity was ample.
already_announced_exclusion: The existing manufacturing-network optimisation, plant closures, support-function efficiencies and other restructuring measures disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Powerful revenue, profit and margin recovery provides very strong contrary evidence. Working-capital absorption, near-zero free cash flow and higher debt create moderate cash pressure, tempered by low leverage and very high interest cover.

source_title: Vesuvius Annual Report and Financial Statements 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 80 and 158 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board and Directors on 28 February 2024; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue fell 5.7% to £1,929.8m, trading profit declined 11.8% to £200.4m, return on sales contracted 70bps to 10.4% and profit before tax fell 13.2% amid difficult second-half markets. However, free cash flow increased to £128.2m, cash conversion reached 93%, net debt fell to £237.5m and leverage remained low at 0.9x. Management described 2023 as the second-most profitable year in the Group's history.
already_announced_exclusion: The announced £30m cost-saving programme, operational-improvement, lean, automation, digitalisation and manufacturing-footprint optimisation measures are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Market weakness and double-digit profit decline create material pressure. Strong cash generation, falling debt, low leverage and still-high absolute profitability provide substantial contrary evidence.
